The Ministry of Health has confirmed a second case of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease in Kenya, noting that health teams detected the infection while the patient was already undergoing mandatory daily monitoring in quarantine.

NAIROBI, Kenya, October 14 – Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola (Bundibugyo virus disease), involving a 39-year-old man who is a close family member of the first patient who died, the Ministry of Health has announced.
The patient, a 39-year-old male and close relative of Kenya’s index Ebola patient, developed a high fever, fatigue, and joint pains on October 13.
The man was already in quarantine under daily monitoring when he developed fever, fatigue and joint pains on October 13.

In an official statement released on Wednesday, October 14, health officials attributed the prompt diagnosis to rigorous daily surveillance, bringing Kenya’s cumulative tallies to two confirmed cases and one death.
Contact tracing teams following the initial infection identified 128 potential contacts.
By October 13, surveillance officers successfully located 113 individuals, placing 108 into a 21-day facility quarantine involving twice-daily clinical reviews and temperature screenings.
By October 13, authorities had traced 113, including 108 who are in quarantine in Kenya and undergoing daily clinical and temperature checks for 21 days.
The National Assembly has unanimously passed the Breastfeeding Mothers Bill, 2024, securing legislative protection for lactating mothers who feed their children at work or in public spaces.

NAIROBI, Kenya, Oct 14 – The National Assembly has passed the Breastfeeding Mothers Bill, 2024, seeking to strengthen the rights of breastfeeding mothers through mandatory lactation facilities, nursing breaks and more flexible working arrangements.

Violators face harsh penalties for interfering with these rights, with statutory default penalties extending to default offenses under the act: “A person convicted of an offense under this Act for which no penalty is provided shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding one million shillings or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or to both.

KISUMU, Kenya, Oct 15 — The government is expanding technology-based learning in schools, targeting more than 20,000 institutions in two phases as it seeks to bridge the digital divide and equip learners with skills for an increasingly technology-driven economy.

The Government is targeting April 2027 to equip all public junior schools in Kenya with digital learning equipment, building on a programme that has so far reached 10,382 schools and trained more than 64,000 teachers.

Principal Secretary for Children Services Caren Ageng’o said 64,000 teachers had been trained nationally to integrate digital tools into classroom instruction, as the government rolls out the National Digital Class Experience under the Digital Literacy Programme (DLP).
The initiative is targeting 10,383 schools in the current phase, with another 10,383 expected to benefit in the second phase, according to the PS.
The 10,382 schools already equipped represent progress towards the April 2027 deadline.

The target featured during President William Ruto’s development tour of the North Rift on its third day, when education infrastructure and digital learning formed part of wider development engagements in Trans Nzoia County.
